title: Reduce observability-agent syscall and allocation overhead via batched sample commits and zero-copy metadata
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: The observability agent (host/sidecar) currently performs per-request sample-decision commits and span-metadata writes that incur frequent syscalls and memory copies on high-QPS services. This contributes to ~6-9% CPU overhead and long-tail latency variance under peak load. Goal: Implement a low-risk, deployable change that batches sampling decisions and metadata commits on the hot path and introduces zero-copy span references to eliminate unnecessary allocations and syscalls, reducing overhead to <=1.5% CPU on representative workloads.

Scope: agent-side batching, collector acceptor changes to handle batched commits, compatibility shim for older collectors, feature flag, extensive load testing and canary rollout. Excludes UI/dashboard changes and end-to-end story for tracing storage.

Success metrics: 1) End-to-end p95 latency for high-QPS proxy path not regressing beyond 5% vs baseline. 2) Agent CPU overhead <=1.5% on standard benchmark (httperf+open-requests test harness). 3) Allocation rate reduced by >=60% measured by jemalloc and runtime metrics. 4) No increase in dropped spans beyond existing baseline (+/-1%).
comments: 2026-02-19 - Maya Chen: Spike complete. Prototype batches sample decisions in a 10ms window before committing to collector; saw syscall reduction from 4300/s to 420/s on a 10k RPS harness.
2026-02-24 - Diego Alvarez: Reworked zero-copy span refs to use arena-backed lifetime tied to request context. Need review from runtime team for safety across async workers.

2026-03-02 - Priya Nair (Runtime): Reviewed API; approved arena approach but requested explicit defensive checks for long-lived spans to avoid memory leak. Added note to implement max-lifetime cutoff (configurable).
2026-03-06 - QA: Load tests show a regression with trace propagation headers over HTTP/2 when batching window is >25ms. Investigating header flush timing; reduced default window to 10ms for now.

2026-03-11 - Diego Alvarez: Created PR github.com/redwood-inference/obs-agent/pull/812 — implements batching with graceful fallback to per-request commit when collector responds with non-200. Added compatibility tests in test/compat/collector_v1_sim.py.

2026-03-13 - SRE: Canary in us-west-2 with runtime-2026.03 flag enabled on 5% of hosts. No errors spike after 48h, small drop in CPU usage observed. Next step: increase to 25% and validate downstream ingestion rate.
2026-03-14 - Maya Chen: Updated ticket with rollout plan and risk matrix. Planning a postmortem template in case of regressions.
notes:
Trade-offs considered: 1) Larger batching windows reduce syscalls but increase risk of losing recent spans on crash — mitigated via short default window (10ms) and ephemeral persistence on flush. 2) Zero-copy reduces allocations but makes lifetime management more complex — added max-lifetime cutoff and defensive checks. 3) Backwards compatibility: collectors that don't support batched commit respond with 501; agent falls back to individual commits.

Rollout: feature-flagged canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with metrics gating (CPU, p95, error-rate, dropped-spans).

Open questions: 1) Should we expose batching window as per-service config in Dedicated? 2) Is there value in exposing aggregated sampling stats to Console for debugging?
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarks demonstrate agent CPU overhead <=1.5% on standard 10k RPS test with default window
Allocation rate reduced >=60% compared to baseline run
No regression in p95 latency beyond 5% vs baseline in canary environment
Collector compatibility tests pass (batched and fallback modes)
PR reviewed by Runtime and SRE and merged
Rollout plan documented and QA sign-off obtained
